c.tagline: Where the Congo River meets vibrant Central African culture.

taxi.fareNote: Shared taxis run fixed routes with no meters; agree the fare (roughly 1,000-2,000 XAF in town) before getting in.

emergency.medical: 118 (fire/ambulance); response can be slow — hotels and embassies keep contacts for trusted private clinics

avoid.reason: Stay out of the outer southern districts (Makélékélé/Bacongo fringes) and unlit areas along the riverfront after dark, where street robberies occur.
Avoid photographing government buildings, the port, bridges or anyone in uniform — it can lead to detention — and watch valuables around Marché Total and other markets.

hood_desc: Brazzaville's downtown core along the Congo River, packed with government buildings, banks, and the city's international-standard hotels. Best for business travelers and anyone wanting easy access to embassies, restaurants, and riverside views.

A historic, densely packed quarter famous for its market and namesake school of painting, with lively, gritty street life. Suits budget travelers and culture seekers after an authentic local feel, though it's quieter on safety after dark.

A traditional residential district south of downtown known for its artisan markets and the colonial-era Case De Gaulle building. Good for travelers seeking cultural immersion and lower prices, a bit further from central attractions.

A leafy, mixed residential-commercial area centered on a well-known roundabout, popular with NGO staff and longer-stay visitors. Suits those wanting a quieter base with easy taxi access to the center.
The zone around Maya-Maya International Airport, home to several modern business hotels. Ideal for early flights or short layovers rather than sightseeing.
lodging: Hilton Brazzaville Les Tours Jumelles Hotel & Residences

water.note: Tap water is not safe to drink; stick to bottled water.

transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash (XAF) directly to the driver or conductor; there is no fare card or ticketing system for shared taxis or buses, so agree the price before boarding. Ferry tickets to Kinshasa are bought at the Beach Ngobila terminal.
transit.hours: Shared taxis and buses run roughly 6am-9pm; after dark, book a ride via Yango or arrange transport through your hotel rather than hailing on the street.
transit.note: There is no metro, tram, or urban rail; getting around relies on shared taxis, moto-taxis, a limited municipal bus service, and the Congo Ocean Railway for longer-distance travel to Pointe-Noire.

ferry: Beach Ngobila ferry to Kinshasa, DRC

tip.r: Not deeply embedded in local custom, but rounding up or leaving a small tip at restaurants and upscale hotels is appreciated, especially where a service charge isn't already included.
